text:
alex: Heads-up — spot preemptions in us-west1 spiked overnight, ~18% hour-over-hour on p3-like instances. Costs saved by spot are growing, but churn is causing increased tail latency for some 99p-sensitive routes.
maria: I saw that. Most of the errors are on models/llama-13b:v2 at sequence lengths >1024, so KV cache refill is expensive.
jin: Can we quantify user impact? which customer tiers/routes saw fallbacks?
alex: Traffic analysis: 70% of the affected requests are free-tier + trial keys, 20% mid-tier, 10% enterprise (they have dedicated capacity fallback). Failure mode is long stalls waiting for spot allocation or preemption mid-request causing retriable generation errors.
ops-bot: cluster-health: preemptible-events=23 (last 1h), avg-restart-delay=112s, us-west1-utilization=86%
carla: Proposed approach: mixed-capacity pools + short warm standby (keep small pool of on-demand per-region) + proactive re-routing to alternate region before retry. That way trials stay cheap but don't blow 99p.
sam: Agree but need routing policy by customer tier. Trials -> prefer spot in-region, fallback -> other region spot -> on-demand warm pool -> dedicated (if enterprise contract). Must preserve SLOs for paid tiers.
maria: Also want model-variant fallback: if quantized variant is available (8-bit) -> use it when capacity is constrained, with a downstream quality tag in response headers for tracking.
jin: Technical notes: prefix caching reduces cost but cache misses on long prefixes amplify preemption pain. Suggest we checkpoint KV cache externally for warm-restores? That gets tricky with privacy.
carla: How about preempt handling: on preempt event, we respond with a 425 (too early) equivalent for streaming requests to let clients reconnect to a different host, and mark token offset so resume is possible.
alex: Good idea. Also need a routing config example. Draft YAML:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  - name: trial_spot_pref
    match: { customer_tier: trial }
    prefer: [us-west1.spot, us-east1.spot]
    fallback_sequence: [us-west1.on-demand-warm, region:nearest.on-demand]
  - name: paid_priority
    match: { customer_tier: paid }
    prefer: [regional.on-demand-warm, regional.spot]
    fallback_sequence: [dedicated_pools, cross-region:on-demand]
  - name: enterprise
    match: { customer_tier: enterprise }
    prefer: [dedicated_pools]
    fallback_sequence: [on-demand-warm]
````
jin: Minor syntax tweak but overall fine. We should include model_variant hints in route selection (e.g., prefer: llama-13b-q8 if latency constrained).
sam: Cost projections: if we keep 5–10% on-demand warm buffer per region (2 GPUs regionally), cost increases ~7% but 99p latency improves dramatically. Worth it for conversion.
maria: Ops checklist: (1) enable preempt handler to persist minimal KV checkpoint, (2) add model-variant tagging + quality header, (3) implement routing policy with tiered fallbacks, (4) telemetry to measure resume success and quality delta.
carla: Can someone run a failover sim next week? I can script spot-kill + route-eval with load.
alex: I'll own the sim, please attach the test plan to the #eng-infra-runbooks page.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: created rolling job preempt-sim/2024-03-12 by alex, status=queued
jin: One more: we need alerting thresholds for spot churn per-region (e.g., >10% preemptions sustained 30m) to trigger automated warm-pool spin-up.
sam: +1. Also add budget guardrails so warm-pool auto-scale has caps by account to avoid runaway costs.
maria: I'll draft PR for routing + telemetry. Expect initial config + unit tests by EOD Friday.
alex: Thanks all — main action items: PR from maria, sim by carla, alert thresholds by jin, budget caps by sam. Follow-up sync Fri 10:30. :thumbsup:
